html:
Brittany is the peninsula at the north-west tip of France, ruled as a kingdom and then a duchy from the 800s until it was joined to France in 1532. It is on the map from 800 to 1530.

The Romans called the region Armorica. In the 400s and 500s Britons crossed from Britain and settled there, and it took their name. They brought the Breton language, a cousin of Welsh and Cornish that is still spoken.

Under the Carolingians Brittany was a border march. Its ruler Nominoe beat the Frankish king at Ballon in 845, and for a time his family ruled as kings. Vikings overran the land in the early 900s; Alan Barbetorte drove them out in the 930s and ruled as duke.

For the next five centuries the dukes steered between their two big neighbours:

  • In the 1100s Brittany fell under the sway of the Angevin kings of England.
  • In the Hundred Years' War two claimants fought the War of the Breton Succession, one backed by France and one by England.
  • The dukes of the later Middle Ages ran an almost independent state with their own coinage and court.

The last duchess, Anne of Brittany, married two kings of France in turn. Her daughter's marriage brought the duchy to the French crown, and the union was made formal in 1532. Brittany kept its own Estates and law courts until the French Revolution swept them away.
sum: Brittany is the peninsula at the north-west tip of France, ruled as a kingdom and then a duchy from the 800s until it was joined to France in 1532. It is on the map from 800 to 1530.
